text: My entire life changed when I realized that the people I admired were just the ones who had the courage to start. The ones who didn't overthink it. Who put their ego aside. Who walked toward uncertainty. Who kept showing up. The answer is found in the action.

The older I get, the more I realize you can get pretty damn far in life by just doing what most people avoid. Wake up early. Focus deeply. Move your body. Eat real foods. Obsess over one thing. Have difficult conversations. Slow down. Be present. It's the recipe for a good life.

Whatever you're doing, do it well. If you're writing a thank you note, take an extra minute to mention something beyond the typical thank you. If you're exercising, do each set as well as you can. If you're in conversation, really listen and don't just wait for your turn to talk.

Having high standards adds up. You can nearly always find an extra minute to do it better. And most important, you prove to yourself that you're the type of person who does things well.

title: No "Zero Days"
text: No day should pass without some contribution to your objectives, however small it may be. Can't do a whole workout? Do 1 push-up. Can't meditate for 30 minutes? Sit for 1 minute.
source: "The Most Useful Life Hacks I've Found In 2026" by Colby Kultgen

title: The "Reverse Bucket List"
text: Create a list of things you've already achieved and experienced—things that you feel proud of. Look at your list on tough days to remind yourself of all the wonderful moments you've lived through.
source: "The Most Useful Life Hacks I've Found In 2026" by Colby Kultgen

title: The "Tell Them" Theory
text: Think the waiter was friendly? Tell them. Your friend looks great today? Tell them. Someone's work inspired you? Tell them. Appreciation costs almost nothing, and people hear far less of it than they deserve.
source: "The Most Useful Life Hacks I've Found In 2026" by Colby Kultgen (h/t Vex King)

title: The power of a 20-minute walk
text: Research shows that a quick, phone-free walk boosts focus, clears your mind, and sharpens your thinking. In one study, kids who took a 20-minute walk before a test scored higher in comprehension, spelling, and math—proof that even a little movement goes a long way for our brains.
source: "The Most Useful Life Hacks I've Found In 2026" by Colby Kultgen

text: Stop being patient and start asking yourself: How can I accomplish my 10 year plan in 6 months? You will probably fail, but you'll be far ahead of the person who simply accepted it would take 10 years.

As I grow older, my tolerance for bullshit has become very thin. I want good people. Good vibes. No pretending. No drama. I want real. Show me who you are. No masks, nothing. Real and raw. That's all. And trust me, I'll get it.

The older I get, the more I realize the beauty in being a regular somewhere. Local coffee shop. Gym. Small restaurant. Whatever. There's something special about the way these third spaces create a feeling of belonging. Real community. It's deeply human and seriously underrated.

Life doesn't pause while you figure it out.

Upgrade every day, or stay married to the mindset that built this version of you.

Nobody is handing you a better life. Not your parents. Not a partner. Not a lucky year.

You build it, or you keep explaining why you didn't.

The hardest part of changing is that people may keep treating you like the person you used to be. Stay with it. Eventually, your new actions become your new reputation, and there is something incredible about watching that happen.

The person you will be in 5 years depends on:

- books or articles you read
- how much more you write
- money you save and invest
- who you work with
- friends you spend time with
- new skills you develop
- the food you eat
- amount of exercise you do
- how much sleep per day
- asking for help when you're stuck
- connections you make and keep
- promises you make and keep
- where and how far you travel
- doors you open for others
- knowing when to leave
- new habits you develop
- quitting the stuff that holds you back
A person's capacity for growth is directly linked to how much truth they can handle about themselves without running away.
The primary purpose of therapy is to help us become aware of the unconscious parts of our mind, accept them, and then begin exerting control over them.
Do not use your energy to worry. Use your energy to believe, to create, to learn, to think and to grow.

title: Use money to gain control over your time
text:
The highest form of wealth is the ability to wake up every morning and say, "I can do whatever I want today." People want to become wealthier to make them happier. Happiness is a complicated subject because everyone's different. But if there's a common denominator in happiness—a universal fuel of joy—it's that people want to control their lives. The ability to do what you want, when you want, with who you want, for as long as you want, is priceless. It is the highest dividend money pays.

Use money to gain control over your time, because not having control of your time is such a powerful and universal drag on happiness. The ability to do what you want, when you want, with who you want, for as long as you want to, pays the highest dividend that exists in finance.
source: The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel

text: Detachment is the path to freedom. Nothing is ever yours to keep. There is nothing you can lose because nothing belongs to you. You did not lose love; you let go of love that was never yours to hold. You did not lose happiness; it comes and goes because it is temporary. Everything changes. Holding on to what cannot be held guarantees pain. Fear, anxiety, and suffering grow from attachment, from trying to hold on to people, patterns, and outcomes. When you feel as though you lose, you are only releasing the illusion of ownership. There is nothing to possess but everything to experience. Accepting impermanence creates space to observe without suffering, to act without fear, and to live. You are free when you let go of the need to control what you cannot.

Underrated life advice: Always default to praise of people who aren't in the room. The way you talk about someone who's not in the room is a loud signal about the energy you carry. Say something kind. Specific. Or nothing at all. Negativity does more harm to you than anyone else.
Read the greats in math, science, and philosophy. Ignore your contemporaries and news. Avoid tribal identification. Put truth above social approval.
context: Answer to the question "What can I do for the next sixty days to become a clearer, more independent thinker?"
source: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant, p. 118

text: No matter how isolated you are and how lonely you feel, if you do your work truly and conscientiously, unknown friends will come and seek you.

title: Your goal in life should be to reduce the amount of time it takes you to get out of a bad state.
text:
Earlier this week I read a line that stood out to me, "Your goal in life should be to reduce the amount of time it takes you to get out of a bad state."

The ability to bounce back quickly is a key skill in life.

My wife once told me, "When you're five, you can be mad for a day. When you're ten, you can be mad for an hour. By the time you're thirty, you get ten minutes—and then you have to move on."

Life is full of moments of frustration and disappointment. Growth and maturity is learning to pull yourself out of a bad state faster.

title: Kaizen — "Improve continuously"
text:
Kaizen is a Japanese concept of continuous improvement through small, consistent steps. It emphasizes patience, discipline, and steady progress over sudden change.

Rather than seeking perfection overnight, kaizen is about getting a little better each day.
note: The original image shows the characters 我慢 ("gaman", enduring with patience) above the title; kaizen is written 改善.

text: You can't control how people perceive you. Someone thinks you're cringe. Someone thinks you're genius. Someone will say you've changed. No matter what you do, someone will have an opinion. None of them are paying your bills. Only you know what's best for you. Just you. So stop performing for an audience that doesn't matter. Let them talk. Just do your thing.

Intelligent people hate pretending. Forced connections. Fake energy. Surface-level conversations. Pretending to be interested in things they don't care about. Performing a personality just to fit in. That shit drains them. They'd rather be alone than "pretend" to be someone they're not.
People rarely succeed unless they have fun in what they are doing.
